title: Closing entries
log: 2026-11-01T14:46:34Z match: Claude Haiku 5.5 found no bank point the same, so it is written new

match.reason: None of the bank points teaches closing entries; they cover the capital account in economics, what accounting is, profit, and profitability ratios, so the closing of revenue and expense accounts to a Profit and Loss Summary needs a new point.

draft.title: Closing entries
card: Revenue and expense accounts are temporary. At the end of the period they are closed, so each starts the next period at zero.
Each revenue account is debited and each expense account is credited, for its balance. The matching entries go to the Profit and Loss Summary account.
Credits in the Profit and Loss Summary (revenue) less debits (expenses) give the profit. A profit is transferred by debiting Profit and Loss Summary and crediting Capital.
Drawings, which are the owner's withdrawals, are closed by debiting Capital and crediting Drawings.
draft.remember: Revenue and expenses close to Profit and Loss Summary. Profit and drawings then go to Capital.

a.q: At the end of the year, Sales revenue has a credit balance of $80,000. What is the closing entry for this account?
opts: Debit Sales, credit Profit and Loss Summary
Debit Profit and Loss Summary, credit Sales
a.why: A credit balance is cleared by a debit, so Sales is debited. The credit goes to Profit and Loss Summary. Revenue is not sent straight to Capital, because profit is worked out first.
a.clue: To clear a credit balance, do the opposite.

b.q: Tom's Tiles has a profit of $30,000 in Profit and Loss Summary. Tom took $12,000 in drawings. How are these closed to Capital?
b.why: Profit increases the owner's equity, so Capital is credited $30,000. Drawings reduce it, so Capital is debited $12,000. The net effect is a $18,000 rise, but each is still closed with its own entry.
b.clue: Profit adds to Capital and drawings take away from it.

a.best: Debit Sales, credit Profit and Loss Summary
